sights.address: Tusculum Ave & Sachem Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45226
sights.w: Cincinnati's oldest neighborhood (settled 1788) and its answer to San Francisco: a cluster of vividly painted Victorian 'Painted Ladies' perched above the Ohio around Tusculum & Sachem, in the old German truck-farming pocket once nicknamed Wooden Shoe Hollow.
sights.k: A residential streetscape — admire from the public sidewalk; these are private homes.

sights.w: A castellated 'castle' gateway at the Eden Park entrance, built 1883 by the Cincinnati Water Works as a valve house and styled after Kronborg (Hamlet's Elsinore) after officials saw a Shakespeare production; on the National Register since 1980.

Billed as the world's largest collection of artists under one roof — 200+ working studios filling a former OTR/Pendleton factory, thrown open to the public on Final Friday (and other Fridays) each month.
sights.k: Studios open mainly Fri evenings (Final Friday 5–9); some by appointment.

sights.w: A hushed 113-acre old-growth ravine forest along the Ohio in the far east end, laced with hilly, bridge-crossed trails and a nature center — one of the city's wildest in-town hikes.
sights.k: Free; trails dawn–dusk (road can flood when the creek rises).

sights.w: A 90-acre Clifton green space hugging the University of Cincinnati, with a fishing lake, disc-golf course, historic bandstand and the Trailside Nature Center's Wolff Planetarium — the oldest planetarium west of the Alleghenies.
sights.k: Free; open 6a–10p. Designated an Audubon Important Bird Area.

sights.w: A Great Parks lake, gorge trail and gardens in Sharonville wrapped around Heritage Village Museum — a dozen relocated 19th-century Southwest-Ohio buildings staffed by costumed interpreters for a living-history walk.
sights.k: Great Parks vehicle pass required; museum has seasonal/limited hours.

sights.w: A 275-acre wooded estate in Amberley Village — bequeathed by printer Herbert Greer French in 1942 — with a hilltop brick manor, a fossil-rich creek and quiet, hilly hiking trails.
sights.k: Free; the French House is a rentable event venue.

sights.w: The Aronoff Center's free, street-level contemporary gallery — Cincinnati's premier showcase for emerging and established local and regional artists across all media.
sights.k: Free admission; open around Aronoff performance hours — check the schedule.

sights.w: A free contemporary-art museum threaded through a boutique hotel in the 1912 Neoclassical Hotel Metropole (on the National Register) — rotating exhibitions open to the public 24/7, plus roaming site-specific installations and the signature yellow penguins.
sights.k: Museum is free and open around the clock; docent tours on select days.

sights.w: A free museum in the Pendleton headquarters of the Verdin Company (bell- and clockmakers since 1842), telling the story of the family firm that has cast and installed bells and street clocks worldwide.
sights.k: Free; small — call ahead for hours.

sights.w: A 300-acre Great Parks riverside meadow in Linwood along the Little Miami, with paved multi-use trails linking to the Lunken Airfield loop, a big dog park and canoe access — prime flat cycling and birding.
sights.k: Free; open green floodplain — trails connect to the Lunken loop.

sights.n: American Legacy Tours — Queen City Underground
sights.w: The signature walking tour into Over-the-Rhine's pre-Prohibition brewing world — subterranean lagering tunnels, a former crypt and the Gateway saloon district; voted Best Historical Tour by Cincinnati Magazine and a USA Today top-five underground tour.
sights.k: Guided tour; tickets and set departure times — book ahead.

sights.address: 10021 Lower River Rd, Rabbit Hash, KY 41005
sights.w: A c.1831 riverfront general store — the best-preserved country store in Kentucky and a National Register hamlet famous for electing a dog as honorary mayor; rebuilt faithfully after a 2016 fire and reopened in 2017.
sights.k: ~40-min drive down the Ohio into Boone County, KY; live music weekends.

sights.n: Big Bone Lick State Historic Site
sights.w: The 'Birthplace of American Vertebrate Paleontology' — Ice Age salt-sulfur bogs that trapped mammoths and mastodons, excavated for Jefferson by William Clark in 1807; today a living bison herd, trails and a free museum, named a National Historic Landmark in 2024.
sights.k: Free museum; ~35-min drive into Boone County, KY.

sights.w: The largest and best-preserved prehistoric hilltop enclosure in North America — 18,000+ feet of Hopewell-built earthen walls above the Little Miami, inscribed in 2023 as part of Ohio's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, with an on-site museum.
sights.k: ~40-min drive to Warren County; Ohio History Connection site with seasonal hours.

sights.w: A three-course dinner aboard restored 1947–1960 streamliner dining cars, rolling from Bond Hill along the Eastern Ave riverfront to the Montgomery Inn Boathouse and back, with period music — nostalgic rail dining that returned after a COVID hiatus.
sights.k: Runs most Saturdays year-round (dark Jan–Feb); reservations required.

sights.address: 251 Mt. Echo Park Dr, Cincinnati, OH 45205
sights.w: An 84-acre Price Hill hilltop park with one of the West Side's most dramatic overlooks of downtown, the Ohio River and Kentucky, anchored by a 1928 Italian Renaissance pavilion — a favorite golden-hour perch.
sights.k: Free; open daily. Pavilion is reservable.

sights.w: A small East Price Hill overlook marking the top of the 1874–1943 Price Hill Incline, with a paved path, benches and a historical marker framing a panorama of the river, downtown and Northern Kentucky.
sights.k: Free; open daily. A viewpoint stop, not a full park.

sights.n: St. Francis de Sales Church & 'Big Joe' Bell
sights.w: A soaring 1879 Gothic Revival church at Madison & Woodburn in East Walnut Hills, home to 'Big Joe' — the largest swinging bell ever cast in the United States (~17.5 tons, cast in Cincinnati in 1895), whose first peal reportedly cracked neighborhood windows.
sights.k: Active parish; interior viewable around services.

sights.w: The walkable heart of trendy Oakley — a triangular business district of boutiques, restaurants and Aglamesis Bros. ice cream, anchored by the neon-marqueed 1941 20th Century Theater (National Register), now a concert and events venue.
sights.k: Stroll the square; the theater is event-only — check listings.

sights.w: Cast in France for the millennium, this 66,000-lb (33-ton) bell was the world's largest free-swinging bell when first rung on Jan 1, 2000, its peal carrying up to 25 miles — the centerpiece of downtown Newport's Millennium Monument.
sights.k: Note: moved into storage in 2024 for adjacent construction; Newport plans to reinstall it at a prominent site — confirm it is on display before making a special trip.
